evals.prompt: Go through evals/files/scrub/handler.go and scrub the useless comments. Language is Go, the exempt directives are //go:* and //nolint, and `go build ./...` is the verify command. Show me what you deleted, trimmed, and kept, with the category for each.
evals.expected_output: A per-comment decision table (delete/trim/keep + category 1-5) and the cleaned file; directive and exported-doc comments untouched.
expectations: Every comment block in handler.go gets exactly one of delete / trim / keep with a category number 1-5
The `//go:generate` and `//nolint` lines are kept and listed as exempt, not scored
The doc comment on the exported `Serve` function is kept (Go tooling enforces exported docs) even though it is tautological
The `// increment i` and `// ---------- helpers ----------` comments are deleted (categories 1 and 5)
No code lines are modified, only comment lines

evals.prompt: my python service in evals/files/scrub/ has a ton of leftover chatgpt-style comments. can you decide which ones to rip out? python, exempt `# noqa` and `# type:`, verify with `python -m py_compile`
evals.expected_output: Decisions per comment block; the `# noqa` / `# type:` lines are exempt; multi-line docstrings on public functions are trimmed rather than deleted.
expectations: `# noqa` and `# type:` comments are reported as exempt and left in place
The 'Step 1:/Step 2:/Step 3:' numbered narration comments are flagged as category 2 (LLM-generated) and deleted
Public function docstrings are trimmed or kept, never deleted outright
Output distinguishes trim from delete and shows the trimmed text for each trim
